champion: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis
ordered_diagnoses: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis

facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
a 4 × 4 cm hard lump in the lower inner quadrant fixed to the chest wall
a firm, mobile 1 × 1 cm lump in the lower outer quadrant
MRI showed a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy
a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern (< 6% probability of malignancy)
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy
poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli
infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive

concepts.why: The patient has a 4 × 4 cm hard lump in the left breast with poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells and pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli, which is consistent with infiltrative ductal carcinoma.
The patient has a firm, mobile 1 × 1 cm lump in the right breast with a well-defined lesion and a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern, which is consistent with fibroadenoma.
The patient has type 2 diabetes, which is a metabolic condition.
The patient has hypertension, which is a cardiovascular condition.

concepts.preferred_label: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis
aliases: Breast Cancer with Lymph Node Involvement
concepts.why: The patient has bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy and malignant cells in the left axillary lymph node, which is consistent with breast cancer with axillary lymph node metastasis.
The patient has infiltrative ductal carcinoma that is estrogen-receptor positive, which is a subtype of breast cancer.
The patient has infiltrative ductal carcinoma that is progesterone-receptor positive, which is a subtype of breast cancer.
The patient has a firm, mobile 1 × 1 cm lump in the right breast with a well-defined lesion and a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern, which is consistent with a benign breast condition.

rationales.F06: The presence of a hard lump fixed to the chest wall is highly suggestive of malignancy.
rationales.F08: The MRI findings of a spiculated mass are highly suspicious for malignancy.
rationales.F11: The cytology results showing poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism and hyperchromasia are indicative of malignancy.
rationales.F12: The core-needle biopsy confirming infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that is estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive provides strong evidence for this diagnosis.
